name: Lip balm / tinted lip color
lead: Lip balm is a wax-like product that moisturizes and protects dry or chapped lips by forming a barrier layer. Tinted versions add color for a natural lip shade.[1] Common bases include beeswax, candelilla and carnauba wax, lanolin, paraffin and petrolatum, sometimes with sunscreen, flavoring or dyes.[1]
In looksmaxxing discussion, it is mentioned as a cheap way to keep lips smooth and add healthy color. Evidence for appearance benefits beyond hydration is limited.

paras: Balms are applied by finger or from a tube. Ingredients may include camphor, cetyl alcohol, sunscreen, flavors and fragrance.[1]

Egyptians made lip care from beeswax, olive oil and animal fat. Charles Browne Fleet developed ChapStick in the 1880s and sold it in 1912, Carmex was created in 1937, flavored balm (Lip Smackers) arrived in 1973, and Burt's Bees launched in 1991.[1]

Some physicians have suggested balms can be addictive or drying, but experts disagree. Dermatologists say irritating ingredients or fragrances may cause problems, and flavors can encourage lip licking.[1] A 2015 German consumer group test found mineral oil hydrocarbons in some products.[1]
Discussions describe balm or tint as a basic grooming step for lip appearance. No community-specific protocols are documented here.

A study in the Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology reported that consistent use improved lip condition and hydration for about eight hours; it was funded by Burt's Bees.[1] No studies were found on tinted balms and perceived attractiveness.

lore.intro: Lip care is a minor topic in grooming discussion, usually as a routine step.

claims.claim: Regular lip balm keeps lips looking healthier and fuller.
